title: Repo settings apply names the missing App permission on a 403
body: Evidence 2026-11-18: `krn repo settings --apply` on KRN exited 69: `gh api -X PATCH repos/{owner}/{repo}` failed with "Resource not accessible by integration (HTTP 403)" because scripts/app-bin/gh forces the GitHub App token, which lacks the Administration permission; the lead applied the gap with the operator account (`env -u GH_TOKEN /usr/bin/gh api -X PATCH ...`) and `krn repo settings` then printed PASS.

Outcome: on a 403 from the App token, `krn repo settings --apply` names the missing App permission and the remedy (grant Administration: write to the App, or rerun with the operator gh login) instead of a bare gh error, and exits with a named code.
Proof: a test with a captured 403 reply asserts the message names the Administration permission and the operator-login remedy.
